# @nucleux/attachments

Attachments — upload files, photos, docs for the AI to read — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

## Exports

Built on `@nucleux/attachment` (`Attachment`, `AttachmentGroup`).

- **`Attachments`** — the root: holds `items`, checks limits before upload (`accept`, `maxSize` bytes, `maxFiles`), owns the file picker, shows refusals in an alert that names the limit, and announces "2 files attached, 1 still being read". Props: `items`, `variant` (`"file-chip"` | `"preview-card"`), `onFilesAdded(files)`, `onFilesRejected(rejections)`, `onRemove(id)`, `onRetry(id)`, `disabled`, `label`.
- **`AttachmentsTray`** — the list of what is in context: chips above the composer, or preview cards.
- **`AttachmentsItem`** — one file. The state is a word first (Uploading 40%, Reading, Ready, Couldn't attach), then size and detail; a hairline bar along its bottom edge is determinate while uploading and indeterminate while reading; a failed file stays listed with **Retry**.
- **`AttachmentsTrigger`** — the add button (icon-only "Attach file", or labelled with children).
- **`AttachmentsDropZone`** — drag-and-drop target that lights up while a file is dragged in (`active` forces it). Standalone it is a dashed box with a "Choose files" button; wrapped around a composer or canvas it covers it only while dragging.
- **`AttachmentsNote`** — says what removal does: forward-only.
- `formatFileSize(bytes)`; types `AttachmentsFile`, `AttachmentsStatus`, `AttachmentsVariant`, `AttachmentsRejection`, `AttachmentsRejectionReason` and each component's Props.

Variants: `file-chip` and `preview-card` are the `variant` prop; `drop-zone-active` is `AttachmentsDropZone`.

Uploading is the app's job: start it in `onFilesAdded`, then feed each item's `status` and `progress` back through `items`.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/attachments @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Attachments, AttachmentsTray, AttachmentsTrigger, AttachmentsNote } from "@nucleux/attachments";

<Attachments
  items={files}
  accept=".pdf,.csv,image/*"
  maxSize={20 * 1024 * 1024}
  maxFiles={5}
  onFilesAdded={upload}
  onRemove={remove}
  onRetry={retry}
>
  <AttachmentsTray />
  <AttachmentsTrigger />
  <AttachmentsNote />
</Attachments>
```

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/autocomplete

Autocomplete — ghost text that anticipates and completes user actions — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

## Exports

- **`Autocomplete`** — a text field (built on `Textarea`) that shows the likely rest of the text as ghost text after the caret.
  - `variant`: `"ghost-suffix"` (inline, with the accept key at its end), `"sentence-completion"` (a whole sentence, with *Tab to accept / Esc to dismiss* hints), `"block-completion"` (multi-line, monospace — code, table rows, long drafts)
  - `getSuggestion(text, { signal })` — the app's model call; returns the continuation (sync or async). Aborted when the text changes. Or pass a fixed `suggestion`.
  - `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange`, `minChars` (8), `debounceMs` (150), `acceptKey` (`"tab"` | `"right"` | `"both"`, never Enter)
  - `onAccept(inserted)`, `onDismiss()`, `onError(error)`, `onStateChange(state)`; `label`, `fieldClassName`, `hideHints`
- Types: `AutocompleteProps`, `AutocompleteVariant`, `AutocompleteAcceptKey`, `AutocompleteState`, `AutocompleteRequest`

## Behaviour

- **Tab** (or the host's key) accepts the whole suggestion as ordinary, editable text and leaves the caret after it. **⌘/Ctrl + →** takes one word. A click on the ghost text accepts it. Accepting never submits.
- **Esc** dismisses it, and it stays away until the field is cleared.
- Keep typing the same words and it follows along without a new request; diverge and it is gone.
- Only suggests once `minChars` are typed and only while the caret is at the end of the text — never mid-word.
- The ghost text lives in an `aria-hidden` overlay, outside the field's value, and is announced once through a polite live region: "Suggestion: …. Tab to accept."
- If `getSuggestion` throws, the field keeps working without a suggestion and `onError` is called.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/autocomplete @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Autocomplete } from "@nucleux/autocomplete";

<Autocomplete
  label="Prompt"
  getSuggestion={async (text, { signal }) => {
    const res = await fetch("/api/complete", { method: "POST", body: text, signal });
    return (await res.json()).completion; // the text to add after the caret
  }}
/>
```

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/caveat

Caveat — says what is incomplete, uncertain or out of date about an AI result — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

## Exports

- **`Caveat`** — a calm reminder that AI output can be wrong, or (better) the specific limitation of this result. `variant`: `below-input` (default caption under the composer) / `output-footer` (filled note under output that will be acted on); `icon` (`null` to omit); `actions` (next steps such as "Review sources"). Rendered as `role="note"`.
- **`CaveatTooltip`** — the `info-tooltip` variant: wraps the generate control (e.g. `Iconography`), shows the caveat on hover and focus, and links it with `aria-describedby`. `content`, `side`, `showIcon`.

Caption-size, muted, never alarming or apologetic; once per surface, repeated only where output will be acted on.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/caveat @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Caveat, CaveatTooltip } from "@nucleux/caveat";
import { Iconography } from "@nucleux/iconography";

<Caveat>Aria may make mistakes. Verify important info.</Caveat>
<Caveat variant="output-footer" actions={<Button size="sm" variant="ghost">Review sources</Button>}>
  2 of 8 interviews could not be opened, so this summary reflects 6.
</Caveat>
<CaveatTooltip content="Output may be inaccurate"><Iconography label="Generate" /></CaveatTooltip>
```

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

# @nucleux/color

Color — a reserved AI accent and working treatment that signals AI is active — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

## Exports

- **`AiColor`** — a surface in the reserved AI accent. `variant`: `accent-border` (default; edge on streaming copy) / `soft-glow` (halo round an active region) / `background-tint` (fill behind AI-generated content); `working` (pulsing ring + streaming caret, `aria-busy`); `label` (the words that travel with the colour, in a polite live region); `asChild`
- **`AiColorHighlight`** — an inline `<mark>` in the accent
- **`AiColorDot`** (`pulse`) — decorative accent dot; always put words beside it
- **`AiColorWorkingRing`** — the "AI is working" treatment as an overlay ring for any `relative` element (used by `@nucleux/agent-avatar`)
- **`aiColorClasses`** — the accent and working classes (`text`, `fill`, `surface`, `border`, `ring`, `working`) on the preset's `brand` tokens

One accent, used sparingly, never alone: pair it with words. All motion stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/color @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { AiColor, AiColorHighlight } from "@nucleux/color";

<AiColor variant="accent-border" working label="Streaming">Analysing your Q2 numbers</AiColor>
<AiColor variant="background-tint" label="Aria suggests">
  Follow up with <AiColorHighlight>Acme Corp</AiColorHighlight> first.
</AiColor>
```

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`

# @nucleux/consent

Consent — asks before the agent accesses something sensitive or acts — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

- **`Consent`** — the `inline-card` request: `title`, `description`, `permissions` (optional; each granted separately), `denyLabel` / `onDeny`, `secondaryLabel` / `onSecondary`, `allowLabel` / `onAllow`, `policyHref` / `policyLabel`

# @nucleux/disclaimer

Disclaimer — a first-impression clarification of what the AI is, isn't, and what it doesn't know — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

A short, honest statement of the agent's scope, limits and knowledge cutoff,
shown at the start of the experience. Not legal boilerplate, and never in the
error colour — a known limit is not a failure.

## Exports

- **`Disclaimer`**
- Types: `DisclaimerProps`, `DisclaimerVariant`, `DisclaimerGroup`

## Variants

| `variant` | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `capabilities-list` (default) | "What Aria can do" on the welcome screen. |
| `limitations-card` | "Aria won't" — regulated or high-stakes contexts. |
| `cutoff-note` | "Aria knows up to April 2026" — a caption in a panel footer or by the compose button. |

## Behaviour

- `agentName` feeds the default title and label; `items` are bullets, `children` a short paragraph.
- Three points max: beyond `maxItems` (3) they sit behind "Show all" (`aria-expanded`).
- `groups` render labelled rows (can / can't / needs approval / may get wrong).
- `cutoff` and `learnMoreHref` add a footer line. The root is `role="note"`, named by its title.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Disclaimer } from "@nucleux/disclaimer";

<Disclaimer agentName="Aria" items={["Summarise documents and threads", "Draft replies and emails"]} cutoff="Apr 2026" />
<Disclaimer variant="cutoff-note" agentName="Aria" cutoff="April 2026" />
```

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/disclaimer @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

```tsx
import { Drawer, DrawerTrigger, DrawerContent, DrawerHeader, DrawerTitle, DrawerDescription, DrawerFooter, DrawerClose } from "@nucleux/drawer";
```

# @nucleux/example-gallery

Example Gallery — a wall of curated outputs that shows users what's possible before they type — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

A clickable set of finished examples. Each card names a real task and what
came back; choosing it hands its prompt to `onSelect` (place it in the
composer — never send it).

## Exports

- **`ExampleGallery`** — the gallery
- **`ExampleGalleryItem`** — one card (a button), for custom layouts
- Types: `ExampleGalleryProps`, `ExampleGalleryItemProps`, `ExampleGalleryExample`, `ExampleGalleryVariant`, `ExampleGallerySelectBehavior`

## Variants

| `variant` | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `card-grid` (default) | A 2–3 column grid filling an empty thread or compose modal. |
| `horizontal-strip` | A scrolling row when vertical space is tight. |
| `categorized-tabs` | Tabs by `category` above the grid. |

## Behaviour

- `examples`: `{ id?, title, description?, prompt, output?, needs?, category?, icon?, preview? }`, capped at `max` (12).
- `selectBehavior="fill"` (default) calls `onSelect(prompt, example)`; `"preview"` opens a Dialog with the prompt and output and a "Use this prompt" button, then returns focus.
- `collapsed` folds it to a "Show examples" button (`onExpand`) once work has started.

## Usage

```tsx
import { ExampleGallery } from "@nucleux/example-gallery";

<ExampleGallery
  examples={[{ title: "Q2 recap", description: "Revenue, churn and wins", prompt: "Summarise Q2…" }]}
  onSelect={(prompt) => setDraft(prompt)}
/>
```

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/example-gallery @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`

# @nucleux/gesture

Gesture Input — swipes, pinches, circles as expressive signals — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/gesture @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { GestureInput } from "@nucleux/gesture";

<GestureInput
  variant="swipe-action"               // "circle-to-select" | "swipe-action" | "pinch-context"
  actions={[
    { gesture: "swipe-left", label: "Summarise" },   // key defaults to ArrowLeft
    { gesture: "swipe-right", label: "File away" },  // key defaults to ArrowRight
  ]}
  onGesture={({ gesture, action, bounds, source }) => run(action)}
  onDismiss={() => {}}
>
  <ThreadCard />
</GestureInput>
```

- **One gesture, one action.** A gesture that maps to no action is reported as not recognised.
- **Recognition:** pass `recognize={(req) => "circle" | … | null}` (sync or async) for your own recogniser;
  otherwise `recognizeSimpleGesture` (exported) reads direction, a closed loop and a two-finger pinch.
- **Feedback:** the live path / swipe offset / zoom follows the pointer; what was captured is outlined,
  labelled (“Circled · Enhance this”) and announced. With `confirm` (default) it waits for the action
  button or Enter, and Escape / Dismiss drops it; with `confirm={false}` it fires and offers Undo.
- **Keyboard equivalents (required):** every action has a key on the focused target (arrows, Enter for
  circle, `+` / `-` for pinch, or `key` for custom gestures) and a visible button.
- Taps pass through to the content; pointer capture starts only once a movement is clearly a gesture.

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/handwriting

Handwriting Input — hand-drawn input recognised as text or instructions — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/handwriting @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { HandwritingInput } from "@nucleux/handwriting";

<HandwritingInput
  variant="draw-pad"                    // "draw-pad" | "live-ocr" | "annotation-stroke"
  convert="review"                      // or "auto" (recognise after a pause)
  onRecognize={async ({ strokes, toImage }) => {
    // Your recogniser — Nucleux never recognises on its own.
    const res = await myRecognizer(await toImage());
    return {
      text: res.text,
      alternatives: res.candidates,     // whole-text readings
      words: res.words,                 // [{ text, uncertain, alternatives }]
    };
  }}
  onAccept={(text, { source, strokes }) => composer.append(text, { from: source, ink: strokes })}
/>
```

- A pointer-driven `<canvas>` pad (pen pressure scales the ink), with **Undo stroke** and **Clear**.
- The reading appears **under** the ink. Words marked `uncertain` are buttons with “?” that open their
  alternatives; **Add to message** stays disabled until they are settled. The reading is editable.
- On failure the ink is kept and **Retry** / **Rewrite** are offered.
- **Type instead** switches to a text field — the keyboard path is always there.
- `annotation-stroke` draws over `children` (a diagram, a screenshot) and reads the mark as an instruction.
- Nothing is sent when writing finishes; `onAccept` hands the confirmed text to your composer.

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/iconography

Iconography — reserved AI action controls: sparkle = generate, refresh = regenerate, wand = transform — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

## Exports

- **`Iconography`** — a Button that runs AI, drawn with the reserved mark for its `intent`: `generate` (sparkle) / `regenerate` (refresh) / `transform` (wand). `label` (the verb, required); `iconOnly` (named "<label> with <agentName>" plus a Tooltip); `agentName`; `tooltip`, `tooltipSide`; `working` + `workingLabel` (mark swaps to the working mark, `aria-disabled`, clicks ignored, announced politely). All Button props (`variant`, `size`, `onClick`…) pass through.

Spec variants: `sparkle-only` = `iconOnly`; `sparkle-label` = `intent="generate"` with a label; `wand-transform` = `intent="transform"`.

Reserve it for actions that call a model — meaning collapses if every button has a sparkle. Glyphs come from `@nucleux/ai-icons` (and honour its `AiIconProvider`).

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/iconography @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

```tsx
import { Iconography } from "@nucleux/iconography";

<Iconography label="Generate" agentName="Aria" iconOnly onClick={generate} />
<Iconography intent="transform" label="Rewrite" variant="secondary"
  working={busy} workingLabel="Rewriting…" onClick={rewrite} />
```

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/initial-cta

Initial CTA — the large, inviting input that anchors the empty state — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

The empty-state invitation: an open headline, at most one supporting line, and
the same `OpenInput` the conversation continues in, so people learn one
control. It composes `SuggestedPrompts` (place, focus, never send) and takes
any other entry point — a `Randomize` dice, say — through `actions`.

## Exports

- **`InitialCta`** (ref → the `<textarea>`)
- Types: `InitialCtaProps`, `InitialCtaVariant`, `InitialCtaHeadingLevel`

## Variants

| `variant` | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `centered-hero` (default) | A wide composer dominating an empty thread. |
| `gradient-cta` | A brand-tinted panel with a single-line composer. |
| `multi-modal-row` | Voice, file and image buttons (`onVoice`, `onAttachFile`, `onAddImage`). |

## Behaviour

- Takes every `OpenInput` prop (`value`/`onValueChange` or `defaultValue`, `onSubmit`, `sendKey`, `maxLength`, `actions`, `loading`…). Uncontrolled, it clears only after a successful send.
- `suggestions` show while the field is empty; choosing one places its prompt, focuses the field with the caret at the end, marks the choice and announces it. They step aside once the person edits, and come back if the field is cleared.
- `headline` (default "What can I help with?") names the section; `headingLevel` sets its level.

## Usage

```tsx
import { InitialCta } from "@nucleux/initial-cta";
import { Randomize } from "@nucleux/randomize";

<InitialCta
  aria-label="Message Aria"
  headline="What can I help with today?"
  description="Ask about your accounts, draft emails, or analyse data."
  suggestions={["Summarise renewal risks", "Draft a follow-up to Acme"]}
  value={draft}
  onValueChange={setDraft}
  actions={<Randomize showLabel={false} prompts={starters} draft={draft} onSelect={(p) => setDraft(p)} />}
  onSubmit={startConversation}
/>
```

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/initial-cta @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/madlibs

Madlibs — a request written as a sentence with a few labelled blanks, filled and reviewed before it goes to the composer — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

A fill-in-the-blank prompt scaffold: "Summarize [document] for [audience], focusing on [topic]." Each blank has a
human label, suggested values and a free-text fallback; an optional clause (`[ … ]`) leaves the sentence while its
blank is empty; the assembled request shows as it fills. An agent-suggested value stays marked until kept. Use prompt
names any missing blank in words (clearing nothing), otherwise hands the sentence to `onUse` for your composer — the
scaffold never sends — and confirms with Undo.

## Exports

- **`Madlibs`** — the scaffold card
- `useMadlibs`, `useMadlibsBlank` — the shared state machine and blank keyboard/ARIA wiring (used by `@nucleux/md3-madlibs`)
- `parseMadlibsTemplate`, `getMadlibsBlanks`, `assembleMadlibsPrompt`, `madlibsBlankWidth` — template helpers
- Types: `MadlibsProps`, `MadlibsBlank`, `MadlibsValues`, `MadlibsSuggestion`, `MadlibsVariant`, `MadlibsBlankStyle`, `MadlibsDensity`, `MadlibsStatus`, `MadlibsPart`, `MadlibsTemplatePart`, `MadlibsController`, `UseMadlibsBlankOptions`

## Variants

| `variant` | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `inline-dropdowns` (default) | A flowing sentence; each blank is an inline field with a list of values |
| `form-rows` | One labelled row per blank, when each slot needs room |
| `chip-builder` | Tap chips to fill the next blank; tap a filled chip to remove it |

`blankStyle` (`filled` / `underline`) and `density` (`comfortable` / `compact`) adjust the look.

## Keyboard

Each blank is an editable combobox: type anything, or ArrowDown/ArrowUp to open and move through its values, Enter to
pick, Escape to close.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/madlibs @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

# @nucleux/mcp-connection

MCP Server Connection — standardised tool access so the AI can act, not just answer — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

## Exports

- **`McpConnection`** — the server card: `name`, `address`, `icon`, `meta`, `status` (`"disconnected"` | `"connecting"` | `"connected"` | `"error"`), `stage` (`"reach"` | `"authenticate"` | `"discover"` — the step in progress or the one that failed), `error`, `account`, `scopes`, and `onConnect` / `onDisconnect` / `onRetry` / `onAuthenticate`. Status is a word plus a dot that is a ring while the server can't be used and filled when it can; the three named steps resolve one at a time; a failed sign-in offers "Sign in again", not a generic retry. Children go in its body.
- **`McpConnectionTools`** (variant `tool-list`) — the tools discovery turned up, grouped least dangerous first: Reads only, Changes things, Destructive. Each row (**`McpConnectionTool`**) shows the human name, the server id, the description, availability as a word (Allowed, Approval required, Off), an optional on/off switch (`onToolEnabledChange`), and expands to inspect the input schema. A failed call shows on its row only. Ends with a trust note: names and descriptions come from the server.
- **`McpConnectionActionPreview`** (variant `action-preview`) — before a tool runs: the call with its arguments, the expected effect, and **Approve / Edit / Never allow**; then running, the result, or the tool's own error ("The server is still connected"). `risk="destructive"` uses the destructive treatment.
- **`McpConnectionPermission`** (variant `permission-toggle`) — "Allow Aria to use Linear?": Always / Just this once / Don't allow, as a radio group. Destructive subjects don't offer Always.
- Types: `McpConnectionStatus`, `McpConnectionStage`, `McpConnectionToolRisk`, `McpConnectionToolAvailability`, `McpConnectionPermissionValue`, `McpConnectionActionStatus`, `McpConnectionToolInfo` and each component's Props.

The component does no networking: the app moves `status` / `stage`, supplies `tools`, and handles every callback.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/mcp-connection @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { McpConnection, McpConnectionTools, McpConnectionActionPreview } from "@nucleux/mcp-connection";

<McpConnection name="Linear MCP" address="https://mcp.linear.app/sse" status={status} stage={stage} onConnect={connect} onDisconnect={disconnect}>
  <McpConnectionTools tools={tools} onToolEnabledChange={setToolEnabled} />
</McpConnection>

<McpConnectionActionPreview
  tool="linear.create_issue"
  args={{ title: "Renewal flow broken", team: "Apollo" }}
  onApprove={run}
  onEdit={edit}
  onDeny={neverAllow}
/>
```

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/md3-autocomplete

Material 3 Autocomplete — ghost text that anticipates and completes user actions — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

The Material 3 twin of [`@nucleux/autocomplete`](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux/tree/main/packages/autocomplete): **same props, callbacks and keyboard model** — switch families by changing only the import. Only the look differs: a filled Material text area (surface-container-high, large shape, primary focus indicator), the suggestion in on-surface-variant fading in over 150 ms (no fade under reduced motion), a small outlined key cap at its end, and assist-chip key hints.

## Exports

- **`Md3Autocomplete`** — a text field that shows the likely rest of the text as ghost text after the caret.
  - `variant`: `"ghost-suffix"`, `"sentence-completion"` (with *Tab to accept / Esc to dismiss* hints), `"block-completion"` (multi-line, monospace)
  - `getSuggestion(text, { signal })` (sync or async, aborted when the text changes) or a fixed `suggestion`
  - `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange`, `minChars` (8), `debounceMs` (150), `acceptKey` (`"tab"` | `"right"` | `"both"`, never Enter)
  - `onAccept(inserted)`, `onDismiss()`, `onError(error)`, `onStateChange(state)`; `label`, `fieldClassName`, `hideHints`, `invalid`
- Types (re-exported from `@nucleux/autocomplete`): `Md3AutocompleteProps`, `Md3AutocompleteVariant`, `Md3AutocompleteAcceptKey`, `Md3AutocompleteState`, `Md3AutocompleteRequest`

## Behaviour

- **Tab** (or the host's key) accepts the whole suggestion as ordinary, editable text and leaves the caret after it. **⌘/Ctrl + →** takes one word. A click on the ghost text accepts it. Accepting never submits.
- **Esc** dismisses it, and it stays away until the field is cleared.
- Keep typing the same words and it follows along without a new request; diverge and it is gone.
- The ghost text lives in an `aria-hidden` overlay, outside the field's value, and is announced once through a polite live region: "Suggestion: …. Tab to accept."

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/md3-autocomplete @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Md3Autocomplete } from "@nucleux/md3-autocomplete";

<Md3Autocomplete
  label="Prompt"
  getSuggestion={async (text, { signal }) => {
    const res = await fetch("/api/complete", { method: "POST", body: text, signal });
    return (await res.json()).completion;
  }}
/>
```

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

A Material 3 Expressive button group: an invisible container that spaces related
buttons and adjusts their shape. The `standard` variant keeps each button's shape
and widens a button while it is pressed; the `connected` variant (the successor to

packages.name: md3-carousel
packages.description:
A Material Design 3 carousel built on Embla. Items are full-bleed tiles with
28px corners and 8px gaps; as they scroll toward the edges they are masked
(clipped symmetrically from both sides, so imagery stays centred) down to a
small sliver, and the following items close up behind them, reproducing the
M3 keyline motion. Four layouts: multi-browse, uncontained, hero (start or
centre aligned) and full-screen. The root is a labelled, focusable
`region` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"`; Left/Right arrows move one
item, Home/End jump to the ends, and each Md3CarouselItem is a labelled
`group` slide ("2 of 6" by default).
packages.summary: Material 3 carousel — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

props.name: Md3CarouselProps

members.name: aria-label
members.description: Accessible name of the carousel region (required).

members.name: layout
members.description: M3 carousel layout. `multi-browse` shows large, medium and small items; `uncontained` keeps every item at full size and lets the last one run off the edge; `hero` shows one large item plus small peek items; `full-screen` shows one item that fills the carousel. Defaults to "multi-browse".

members.name: alignment
members.description: Hero only: put the large item at the start (with a small item after it) or centred between two small items. Defaults to "start".

members.name: itemWidth
members.description: Full-size width of a large item in px, for `multi-browse` and `uncontained`. Defaults to 200.

members.name: smallItemWidth
members.description: Width of a fully masked (small) item in px; M3 allows 40–56. Defaults to 56.

members.name: opts
members.description: Extra Embla options (loop, dragFree…); `axis` and `align` are set by the layout.

members.name: setApi
members.description: Receive the Embla API instance once ready.

members.name: onIndexChange
members.description: Called with the index of the item at the focal position after each snap.

props.name: Md3CarouselItemProps

members.name: label
members.description: Short text shown over the bottom of the item; it fades out as the item is masked.

Material 3 gesture input: turns swipes, circles and pinches on a target
region into AI actions using pointer events. Each gesture maps to one action;
recognition is the app's `recognize` callback or the shared geometric
`recognizeSimpleGesture`. The mark draws in the primary colour as you draw,

Material 3 handwriting input: a pointer-driven writing pad (pen pressure
aware) whose ink the app's own recogniser (`onRecognize`) reads into text.
The reading appears under the ink, never over it; words the recogniser was
unsure of carry a dotted underline and a “?” in the error tone and must be
settled from their alternatives (an MD3 menu) before Add to message is
enabled, and the reading stays editable in an MD3 text field. Undo stroke,

# @nucleux/md3-modes

Material 3 Modes — choose how the agent approaches a request (Brainstorm, Draft, Review, Plan), as a chip in the composer or a Mode row in Request settings, switchable before sending — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

**Same API as the shadcn twin.** The props, callbacks, states, keyboard model and accessible names are those of [`@nucleux/modes`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/modes) (`Modes`) — the props types are re-exported from it and the state logic (`useModes`) is shared — so you switch families by changing only the import. Only the look differs: Material 3 colour roles, shape, elevation, state layers and motion (reduced under `prefers-reduced-motion`). In the `composer` variant the Mode chip sits in an `Md3AgentComposer` toolbar and the picker grows up from the composer.

## Exports

- **`Md3Modes`** — the whole pattern (`variant`: `composer` · `segmented` · `list` · `chip`)
- **`Md3ModesSegmented`** — an `Md3SegmentedButton` of modes (radio group)
- **`Md3ModesList`** — mode rows: 40dp icon tile, name, what changes, unavailable reason, trailing check
- **`Md3ModesChip`** — outlined "Mode ▾" assist chip, or tonal "Mode **Plan** ▾ ×" once set
- **`Md3ModesPicker`** — the menu-surface dialog: heading, rows, error-container alert, "No mode"
- **`Md3ModesNote`** — "Mode changed to … Your text is unchanged." with Undo
- Types: `Md3ModesProps`, `Md3ModeOption`, `Md3ModesVariant`, `Md3ModesNotice`, `Md3ModesSubmitDetails`, and each sub-component's `Md3…Props`

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/md3-modes @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Md3Modes } from "@nucleux/md3-modes";
import { Flag, Lightbulb, NotebookPen, Eye } from "lucide-react";

<Md3Modes
  modes={[
    { id: "brainstorm", name: "Brainstorm", icon: <Lightbulb />, description: "Explore several possible directions." },
    { id: "draft", name: "Draft", icon: <NotebookPen />, description: "Write a first version you can edit." },
    { id: "review", name: "Review", icon: <Eye />, description: "Check existing work for gaps and risks." },
    { id: "plan", name: "Plan", icon: <Flag />, description: "Break the work into steps with owners and dates." },
  ]}
  onSubmit={(text, { mode }) => send(text, { mode: mode?.id })}
/>
```

`sendLabel` is accepted for API parity; the send button is named by `Md3AgentComposer` ("Send").

and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

Material 3 Open Input — the persistent free-form composer for any natural-language ask: grows to eight lines then Expand, with a Request settings menu (Mode, Tone, Style, Improve prompt) — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

**Same API as the shadcn twin.** The props, callbacks, keyboard model and accessible names are those of [`@nucleux/open-input`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/open-input) (`OpenInput`) — the props types are re-exported from it — so you switch families by changing only the import. Only the look differs: Material 3 colour roles, shape, elevation, state layers and motion (reduced under `prefers-reduced-motion`).

## Exports

- **`Md3OpenInput`** — the persistent composer: auto-grows to `maxHeight`, Enter or ⌘/Ctrl+Enter sends (`sendKey`), counter near `maxLength`, keeps the text and offers Retry when `onSubmit` rejects, Stop while `loading`; variants expanding-area / single-line / input-with-send
- Types: `Md3OpenInputProps`, `Md3OpenInputVariant`, `Md3OpenInputSendKey`

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/md3-open-input @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Md3OpenInput } from "@nucleux/md3-open-input";

<Md3OpenInput label="Ask Aria" placeholder="Ask about this project…" onSubmit={send} />
```

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

packages.name: md3-proactive
packages.description:
The Material 3 proactive suggestion — the same API and behaviour as
`ProactiveSuggestion`. The agent leads with the finding, can show the
evidence, and offers exactly one next action (a filled M3 small button
that shows the working mark and `pendingLabel` while `onAction` is
pending), an optional text-button snooze and a dismiss icon button (or
Escape). The contextual banner is a secondary-container card with a
"Suggested by" provenance line; the inline suggestion a single capsule
beside its row; the side toast a level-3 surface in the corner. It rises
in on the emphasized-decelerate curve, is announced politely, and with an
`evidenceKey` a dismissal is remembered for the same facts.

packages.description:
The Material 3 "surprise me" control — the same API and behaviour as
`Randomize`. It sits beside the composer, never replaces it, and sends
nothing: the chosen prompt goes to `onSelect` to be placed in the composer,
editable, and if the composer already holds the person's words it asks
first (Replace, Add below, Cancel) in a level-2 surface. Drawn as a tonal
dice icon button for a composer toolbar, an outlined shuffle bar that

lands. Working uses the M3 loading indicator; no dice animation.

```tsx
  <Md3SideSheetActions>
```

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/md3-split-button @nucleux/md3-menu @nucleux/tokens
```

```tsx
import { Md3SplitButton } from "@nucleux/md3-split-button";
```

# @nucleux/md3-structured-input

Material 3 Structured Input — a compact form for exact values, suggestions marked and every value yours — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

This is the Material 3 twin of [`@nucleux/structured-input`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/structured-input) (`StructuredInput`). It shares the twin's API exactly — the props types are the twin's own — so you can switch families by changing only the import. Only the look differs: MD3 colour roles, shape, elevation, state layers and motion (stilled under reduced motion).

## Exports

- **`Md3StructuredInput`** — a clarifying question as MD3 radio / checkbox rows, free-text escape and skip
- **`Md3StructuredInputSlots`** — 2–4 labelled MD3 outlined fields; “Suggested” marks become “Edited by you”
- **`Md3StructuredInputTags`** — `@` / `p:` / `/` tags become tonal input chips, suggestions as MD3 suggestion chips
- **`Md3StructuredInputWizard`** — multi-step MD3 card with a segmented progress track
- **`structuredPartsToText`** — re-exported from `@nucleux/structured-input`
- Types: `Md3StructuredInputProps`, `Md3StructuredInputSlotsProps`, `Md3StructuredInputTagsProps`, `Md3StructuredInputWizardProps`, `StructuredOption`, `StructuredInputSlot`, `StructuredInputValues`, `StructuredInputTagTrigger`, `StructuredInputPart`

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/md3-structured-input @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Md3StructuredInput } from "@nucleux/md3-structured-input";

<Md3StructuredInput
  question="Which audience is this for?"
  options={[{ value: "execs", label: "Executives" }, { value: "eng", label: "Engineers" }]}
  onSubmit={(values) => answer(values)}
/>
```

packages.name: md3-suggestions
packages.description:
The Material 3 suggestions row — the same API and behaviour as
`Suggestions`: at most three verb-labelled chips above the composer
("compose"), under an answer ("follow-up") or as a floating toolbar on a
selection ("selection"). The row is headed by the agent's mark and name
(`label`, "Aria suggests") with an info icon button that reveals why
(`reason`) and a close icon button (Escape too); compose chips are outlined
M3 suggestion chips with a leading primary add icon and the standard state
layer. Choosing a chip only calls `onSelect` — never sends — and `status`
swaps the row for a one-line confirmation with a text Undo, a dismissed or
no-longer-relevant line, a loading indicator or an error-container line
with Retry. Arrow keys, Home and End move between chips; motion is reduced
under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
packages.summary: Material 3 Suggestions — agent-marked suggestion chips above the composer that add to the request, never send it — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

# @nucleux/md3-suggestions

Material 3 Suggestions — agent-marked suggestion chips above the composer that add to the request, never send it — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

**Same API as the shadcn twin.** The props, callbacks, keyboard model, states and accessible names are those of [`@nucleux/suggestions`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/suggestions) (`Suggestions`, `SuggestionsComposer`) — the props types are re-exported from it and the state logic is shared — so you switch families by changing only the import. Only the look differs: Material 3 colour roles, outlined suggestion chips with a primary add icon, state layers, a raised composer card, and motion reduced under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Exports

- **`Md3Suggestions`** — the "Aria suggests" chip row with Why and Dismiss icon buttons, its status lines (added with Undo, dismissed, no longer relevant, loading, error with Retry), plus `follow-up` and `selection` variants
- **`Md3SuggestionsComposer`** — the row wired to `Md3AgentComposer`

- Types: `Md3SuggestionsProps`, `Md3SuggestionsComposerProps`, `Md3SuggestionItem`, `Md3SuggestionsVariant`, `Md3SuggestionsStatus`, `Md3SuggestionsMessages`

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/md3-suggestions @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Md3SuggestionsComposer } from "@nucleux/md3-suggestions";

<Md3SuggestionsComposer
  defaultValue="Summarize the September release."
  label="Aria suggests"
  reason="Release summaries are read to decide what still needs attention."
  suggestions={[
    { label: "Include unresolved blockers" },
    { label: "Group the work by owner" },
```

packages.description:
A Material 3 Expressive toolbar for actions related to the current page. The
`docked` type spans the bottom (or top) of the screen at 64px tall and replaces
the bottom app bar; the `floating` type is an elevated, fully rounded container
that floats over content in a horizontal or vertical orientation and pairs well

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

This is the Material 3 twin of [`@nucleux/voice-input`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/voice-input) (`VoiceInput`). It shares the twin's API exactly — the props types are the twin's own — so you can switch families by changing only the import. Only the look differs: MD3 colour roles, shape, elevation, state layers and motion (stilled under reduced motion).

## Exports

- **`Md3VoiceInput`** — waveform / mic-button / transcript-stream; a lit secondary mic state over a soft gradient, Pause/Resume, Cancel and Stop (which never sends), an MD3 loading indicator while transcribing
- Types: `Md3VoiceInputProps`, `Md3VoiceInputState`, `Md3VoiceInputVariant`

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/md3-voice-input @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Md3VoiceInput } from "@nucleux/md3-voice-input";

<Md3VoiceInput state={state} duration="0:08" onStart={start} onPause={pause} onConfirm={stop} onCancel={cancel} />
```

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/model-selection

ModelSelection — choose which model handles the generation — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

## Exports

- **`ModelSelection`** — lets the user pick the model for the task. Props: `models`, `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange`, `label`, and
  - `variant`: `"dropdown"` (default — a composer-anchored listbox: arrow keys, Home/End, Escape returns focus to the trigger), `"tradeoff"` (radio cards with speed, quality and cost in human terms), `"auto-route"` (on by default — "Aria picks the model per task", shows `routedModel`; switching it off reveals the dropdown)
  - `autoRoute` / `defaultAutoRoute` (true) / `onAutoRouteChange`, `routedModel`, `agentName`
- **`ModelOption`**: `value`, `label`, `description`, `icon`, plus `recommended` (a "Recommended" badge), `speed`, `quality`, `cost` (human terms, never parameter names), `disabled` with `unavailableReason` (the row stays and says what answers instead).

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/model-selection @nucleux/tokens
```

```tsx
import { ModelSelection } from "@nucleux/model-selection";

  variant="tradeoff"
  defaultValue="sonnet"
  models={[

    { value: "sonnet", label: "Sonnet", quality: "Balanced", speed: "Medium", cost: "$$", recommended: true },
    { value: "haiku", label: "Haiku", quality: "Good enough", speed: "Fastest", cost: "$" },
```

# @nucleux/modes

Modes — choose how the agent works on a request (Fast, Balanced, Deep research), as a chip in the composer or a Mode row in Request settings, switchable before sending — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

A named set of behaviour presets that makes the speed/depth trade-off — or the
way of working — legible without exposing raw parameters. Each mode says what
changes and how long it takes; the active mode sits in the composer as a chip
that can be changed or cleared before sending; unavailable modes stay listed
with the reason; a change adds one quiet line with Undo. Choosing a mode never
touches the prompt text, and Modes never sends on its own.

## Exports

- **`Modes`** — the whole pattern (`variant`: `composer` · `segmented` · `list` · `chip`)
- **`ModesSegmented`** — the segmented control (radio group)
- **`ModesList`** — rich rows: icon, name, expected speed · what it's for, unavailable reason
- **`ModesChip`** — the composer chip ("⚡ Fast ▾") with an optional ×
- **`ModesPicker`** — the dialog the chip opens: heading, rows, refusal alert, "No mode"
- **`ModesNote`** — "Mode changed to … Your text is unchanged." with Undo
- Shared logic (also used by `@nucleux/md3-modes`): `useModes`, `useModesRoving`, `useModesDismiss`, `modesLabels`, `modeSupportingText`
- Types: `ModesProps`, `ModeOption`, `ModesVariant`, `ModesNotice`, `ModesSubmitDetails`, `UseModesOptions`, `ModesState`, and each sub-component's `…Props`

## Variants

| `variant` | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `composer` (default) | The site's live preview: segmented control, the mode list and the chip in the composer. |
| `segmented` | Three or four labelled segments — session-level, like a tab (right rail, code). |
| `list` | Rich rows with expected speed — generation settings. |
| `chip` | Only the chip and its picker — beside the send button (chat, email). |

## Behaviour

- `modes` (`{ id, name, shortName?, description?, meta?, icon?, unavailable? }[]`), `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange(id | null, mode | null)`.
- `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` for the picker; `clearable` (default true); `showDescriptions` (default true); `label` (default "Mode").
- Choosing an `unavailable` mode is refused: it isn't applied, the picker shows why (`role="alert"`), `onUnavailable(mode)` fires.
- Composer: `draft` / `defaultDraft` / `onDraftChange`, `onSubmit(text, { mode })`, `placeholder`, `composerLeading`, `composerActions`, `sendLabel`.
- Keyboard: radio groups with one tab stop; Arrow keys / Home / End move, Space or Enter chooses; Escape closes the picker and returns focus to the chip. Changes are announced politely.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/modes @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Modes } from "@nucleux/modes";

<Modes
  modes={[
    { id: "fast", name: "Fast", icon: "⚡", meta: "~3 seconds", description: "everyday asks and quick lookups" },
    { id: "balanced", name: "Balanced", icon: "⚖️", meta: "~15 seconds", description: "most tasks" },
    { id: "deep", name: "Deep research", shortName: "Deep", icon: "🧠", meta: "~1 minute", description: "multi-source, high-stakes" },
  ]}
  defaultValue="balanced"
  onSubmit={(text, { mode }) => send(text, { mode: mode?.id })}
/>
```

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/nudges

Nudges — tiny contextual hints that surface features the user hasn't discovered yet — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

A small, non-blocking tip shown when a real signal fires. It says what the
person can do, can say why it appeared, and offers Try it, Not now and a
dismiss button (Escape too). With a `nudgeId` it is capped at one per session
and dismissals are remembered.

## Exports

- **`Nudge`** — the tip
- **`NudgeAction`** — a small action button for extra `actions`
- Types: `NudgeProps`, `NudgeActionProps`, `NudgeVariant`, `NudgeSide`, `NudgePersist`

## Variants

| `variant` | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `inline-tip-card` (default) | A card in the layout for less time-sensitive tips. |
| `tooltip-nudge` | A bubble pointing at `children` (the control); closes on outside click. |
| `highlight-pulse` | A soft ring and a "New" badge around `children`, gone once used. |

## Behaviour

- `message` (required), `title`, `reason` (behind "Why this tip?", `aria-expanded`).
- `onTry` / `onSnooze` / `onDismiss` show their actions; `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` control visibility.
- The anchor control gets `aria-describedby` pointing at the message.
- `nudgeId` + `persist` (`"local"` default, `"session"`, `"none"`): a dismissed or used tip never returns, and only one id'd nudge shows per session. `onImpression` fires each time it is shown, for tracking.
- The pulse respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Nudge } from "@nucleux/nudges";

{textOnlySends >= 3 && (
  <Nudge variant="tooltip-nudge" nudgeId="pdf-upload" message="Try uploading a PDF — Aria can summarise it in seconds."
    reason="You've sent three text-only messages." onTry={openUpload} onImpression={track}>
    <Button size="icon" aria-label="Attach a file"><Paperclip /></Button>
  </Nudge>
)}
```

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/nudges @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/open-input

Open Input — free-form composer for any natural-language ask: grows to eight lines then Expand, with a Request settings menu (Mode, Tone, Style, Improve prompt) — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

The persistent composer users return to after the first interaction. It grows
with the prompt up to `maxHeight` and then scrolls, always pairs the field with
a visible send button, shows a counter only near `maxLength`, and never loses
the text: a failed send keeps it and offers Retry.

## Exports

- **`OpenInput`** — the composer (ref → the `<textarea>`)
- Types: `OpenInputProps`, `OpenInputVariant`, `OpenInputSendKey`

## Variants

| `variant` | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `expanding-area` (default) | Starts as one line, grows; controls in a footer row. Chat, email. |
| `single-line` | Compact pill for dense layouts (a docked side panel). |
| `input-with-send` | Field plus a separate, explicit send button. Canvas and code prompts. |

## Behaviour

- `value` + `onValueChange` (controlled) or `defaultValue` (uncontrolled — clears only after a successful send).
- `onSubmit(text)` may return a promise: a spinner shows while pending; a rejection keeps the text and shows an error row (`role="alert"`) with Retry. Pass `error` / `onRetry` to control it yourself.
- `sendKey="enter"` (default; Shift+Enter is a newline) or `"mod-enter"` (⌘/Ctrl+Enter sends). The send button carries `aria-keyshortcuts`.
- Send is disabled only while there is nothing to send. `loading` swaps it for a Stop button (`onStop`).
- `label` renders a visible `<label>`; otherwise pass `aria-label`. `actions` holds secondary controls (add context, voice, model).
- `maxLength` + `counterThreshold` (0.8): the `n / max` counter appears near the limit (`aria-live="polite"`).

## Usage

```tsx
import { OpenInput } from "@nucleux/open-input";

const [value, setValue] = useState("");

<OpenInput
  label="Ask Aria"
  placeholder="What do you want to know?"
  value={value}
  onValueChange={setValue}
  maxLength={4000}
  onSubmit={async (text) => { await send(text); setValue(""); }}
/>
```

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/open-input @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/preset-styles

Preset Styles — one-click named styles for how the agent's output looks or reads, as a chip or a Style row in Request settings — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

A style communicates in one tap what would take a paragraph to describe. Pick
it before generating (a swatch grid or a list of brand presets), or set how
replies are written from the composer's Style control — with a sample reply
that follows the pointer, a chip that names the active style, × back to the
base style with Undo, and custom styles made from the person's own writing.
The request text is never edited: the style travels with the send.

## Exports

- **`PresetStyles`** — the picker (`variant`: `"grid"` | `"list"` | `"menu"`)
- **`usePresetStyles`** — its state and behaviour (shared with the Material 3 twin), plus `presetStylesCopy`, `presetStylesNoticeText` and `presetStylesMoveFocus`
- Types: `PresetStylesProps`, `PresetStyle`, `PresetStylesVariant`, `PresetStylesView`, `PresetStylesNotice`, `PresetStyleSwatch`, `PresetStyleReference`, `PresetStyleRequest`, `PresetStyleDraft`, `PresetStyleSource`

## Variants

| `variant` | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `grid` (default) | Swatch tiles picked before generating; `allowReference` adds "Match a style" (drop or pick an image), `lockable` the per-project lock. |
| `list` | A short list of named, brand-agreed presets. |
| `menu` | A Style control in the composer (`OpenInput`) that opens "Use style": styles with one line each, a live preview, Create & edit styles. |

## Behaviour

- `styles`, `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange`. Arrow keys, Home and End move between styles.
- Grid / list: `lockable`, `locked` / `defaultLocked` / `onLockedChange`, `lockScope`; `allowReference`, `reference` / `defaultReference` / `onReferenceChange(file | null)`.
- Menu: choosing applies at once and closes; Escape or an outside click closes and returns focus to the control. `previewPrompt` + each style's `sample` drive the preview (`showPreview`). One status line says where the style applies (`scope`, `earlierReplies`); × returns to `baseStyle` with Undo.
- Custom styles: pass `onGenerateStyle(request) => Promise<draft>` (the app's model call) to enable Create & edit styles — paste or upload an example, or describe the style; the component shows progress and a retryable error, then a review card where name, description and instructions are editable, with a preview, Save and Save and use (`onSaveStyle(style, use)`).
- `withComposer={false}` renders only the Style control for your own composer; otherwise `message` / `defaultMessage` / `onMessageChange` and `onSubmit(text, styleId)`.

## Usage

```tsx
import { PresetStyles } from "@nucleux/preset-styles";

<PresetStyles
  variant="menu"
  styles={[
    { id: "normal", name: "Normal", description: "Aria’s default replies.", sample: normalReply },
    { id: "concise", name: "Concise", description: "Shorter, more direct replies.", sample: conciseReply },
  ]}
  previewPrompt="Summarize the October release."
  onGenerateStyle={(req) => api.generateStyle(req)}
  onSubmit={(text, style) => send(text, { style })}
/>
```

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/proactive

Proactive Suggestions — invisible AI moments that arrive exactly when needed — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

An unsolicited suggestion raised when the agent notices something specific and
actionable. It leads with the finding, can show the evidence, offers exactly
one next action plus a one-press dismiss (× or Escape) and an optional snooze,
and does nothing until the person acts.

## Exports

- **`ProactiveSuggestion`**
- Types: `ProactiveSuggestionProps`, `ProactiveSuggestionVariant`, `ProactiveSuggestionPersist`

## Variants

| `variant` | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `contextual-banner` (default) | At the top of a surface. |
| `inline-suggestion` | A compact action beside the row or element it is about. |
| `side-toast` | Fixed to the bottom-right corner (override with `className`). |

## Behaviour

- `title` (the finding), `description` (the recommendation), `reason` (the evidence), `actionLabel` + `onAction`.
- `onAction` may return a promise: the action shows a spinner and `pendingLabel` meanwhile.
- `evidenceKey` + `persist` (`"local"` default): a dismissal is remembered so the same facts never bring it back, and only one keyed suggestion shows per session.
- `resolved` says "Resolved" and drops the actions. It sits in a polite live region, so its arrival is announced without taking focus.

## Usage

```tsx
import { ProactiveSuggestion } from "@nucleux/proactive";

<ProactiveSuggestion
  agentName="Aria"
  evidenceKey="renewals-2026-w17"
  title="Three renewals expire this week"
  description="Want Aria to draft outreach for each?"
  actionLabel="Draft emails"
  onAction={openReview}
  onSnooze={remindTomorrow}
/>
```

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/proactive @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

# @nucleux/prompt-enhancer

Prompt Enhancer — a magic-wand action that rewrites a short ask into a precise one, shown as a reviewable diff; starts from the wand or the Improve prompt row in Request settings — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

An Enhance action in the composer expands a terse prompt into a clearer one
and shows it beside the original — each addition marked, explained and
removable, assumptions labelled. It never silently replaces the prompt: Use
puts the result in the composer with Undo and sends nothing; Keep original and
Edit are always there, and a failure leaves the original untouched. The
component calls no model — the app supplies `onEnhance`.

## Exports

- **`PromptEnhancer`** — the composer, the Enhance action and the review
- **`usePromptEnhancer`** — the shared, non-visual logic (state machine, async enhance with cancel, Use/Undo)
- Helpers: `buildEnhancedPrompt`, `resolveEnhancedPrompt`, `getPromptEnhancerSegments`, `describePromptEnhancerChange`, `PROMPT_ENHANCER_TEXT`
- Types: `PromptEnhancerProps`, `PromptEnhancerVariant`, `PromptEnhancerState`, `PromptEnhancerDiffStyle`, `PromptEnhancerChange`, `PromptEnhancerSuggestion`, `PromptEnhancerSegment`, `PromptEnhancerController`

## Variants

| `variant` | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `preview-diff` (default) | Original and enhanced side by side (`diffStyle="split"`) or one sentence with additions marked (`"inline"`) |
| `wand-button` | The enhancement is applied in place; Undo restores the original |
| `auto-enhance-toggle` | A switch: when on, Send enhances the prompt first, then sends it |

States: `original`, `enhancing` (cancel), `enhanced`, `editing`, `accepted` (Undo), `reverted`, `failed` (Try again / Keep original).

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/prompt-enhancer @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { PromptEnhancer } from "@nucleux/prompt-enhancer";

<PromptEnhancer
  value={draft}
  onValueChange={setDraft}
  hint="Aria will expand this prompt"
  onEnhance={(prompt, { signal }) => api.enhance(prompt, { signal })}
  // resolves with { changes: [{ id, text: " from the last quarter", reason, assumption? }] }
  // or { text: "the whole enhanced prompt" }
  onSubmit={send}
/>
```

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

Multi-step questionnaire with single, multiple, freeform and skippable answers — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

```tsx
import { Questionnaire, QuestionnaireProgress, QuestionnaireItem, QuestionnaireTitle, QuestionnaireChoices, QuestionnaireChoice, QuestionnaireInput, QuestionnaireError, QuestionnaireActions, QuestionnairePrevious, QuestionnaireSkip, QuestionnaireNext, QuestionnaireSubmit } from "@nucleux/questionnaire";

  shortcuts="letters"
  onSubmit={(event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const answers = new FormData(event.currentTarget); // answers.get("direction"), answers.getAll("signals")
  }}
>
  <QuestionnaireProgress />
  <QuestionnaireItem name="direction" required>
    <QuestionnaireTitle>What should we prototype next?</QuestionnaireTitle>

      <QuestionnaireChoice value="questions">Question prompts</QuestionnaireChoice>
      <QuestionnaireInput aria-label="Another direction" placeholder="Type another direction…" />

    <QuestionnaireChoices>
      <QuestionnaireChoice value="progress">Progress</QuestionnaireChoice>
      <QuestionnaireChoice value="risks">Risks</QuestionnaireChoice>
    </QuestionnaireChoices>
    <QuestionnaireError />
  </QuestionnaireItem>
  <QuestionnaireActions>
    <QuestionnairePrevious />
    <QuestionnaireSkip />
    <QuestionnaireNext />
    <QuestionnaireSubmit>Save answers</QuestionnaireSubmit>
  </QuestionnaireActions>
</Questionnaire>
```

# @nucleux/randomize

Randomize — a 'dice' that kickstarts the experience with a fun result — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

A "surprise me" control beside the composer that fills it with a random
starter. It never replaces the input and never sends: the prompt goes to
`onSelect`, editable. If the composer already holds the person's words it asks
first — Replace, Add below or Cancel.

## Exports

- **`Randomize`**
- Types: `RandomizeProps`, `RandomizeVariant`, `RandomizeUseMode`

## Variants

| `variant` | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `dice-button` (default) | A dice in the composer toolbar; one tap places a starter (`showLabel={false}` inside a toolbar). |
| `shuffle-bar` | A labelled bar: shuffle, preview, then Use this. |
| `random-card` | A card with a random starter, Pick another, Use this and a way back. |

## Behaviour

- `prompts`: a local pool, no repeats until it is used up. Or `generate(previous)` (sync or async) with a working state ("Finding a different direction…") and Try again on failure.
- `onSelect(prompt, { mode })` — `mode` is `"append"` when the person chose Add below.
- Pass the composer's text as `draft` to enable the replace / add below / cancel guard.
- Status changes are announced politely.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Randomize } from "@nucleux/randomize";

<Randomize
  variant="random-card"
  prompts={["Draft a one-paragraph product brief for an idea you haven't shipped."]}
  draft={draft}
  onSelect={(p, { mode }) => setDraft(mode === "append" ? `${draft}\n\n${p}` : p)}
/>
```

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/randomize @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`

# @nucleux/select

Select — a custom listbox select with a trigger, groups and keyboard navigation — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).


## Exports

- **`Select`** — root; `value`/`defaultValue`/`onValueChange`, `open`/`onOpenChange`, `disabled`, `required`, `name` (submits with forms)
- **`SelectTrigger`** (`size`: default/sm), **`SelectValue`** (`placeholder`)
- **`SelectContent`** — the listbox (`position`, `align`); flips above the trigger when there is no room below
- **`SelectItem`** (`value`, `disabled`, `textValue`), **`SelectGroup`**, **`SelectLabel`**, **`SelectSeparator`**
- **`SelectScrollUpButton`**, **`SelectScrollDownButton`** — kept for shadcn API parity

For a plain native `<select>`, use `@nucleux/native-select`.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/select @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Select, SelectTrigger, SelectValue, SelectContent, SelectItem } from "@nucleux/select";

<Select value={status} onValueChange={setStatus}>
  <SelectTrigger aria-label="Status"><SelectValue placeholder="Status" /></SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent>
    <SelectItem value="open">Open</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="done">Done</SelectItem>
  </SelectContent>
</Select>
```

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/structured-input

StructuredInput — an agent's structured clarifying question — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/structured-input @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

Lightweight slots and hints that compose clearer prompts. Four composable pieces:

```tsx
import {
  StructuredInput,        // a clarifying question with single/multi choice, "something else" and skip
  StructuredInputSlots,   // named-slots: 2–4 labelled fields that fill a prompt template
  StructuredInputTags,    // tag-input: @person, p:project, /file become chips
  StructuredInputWizard,  // wizard-step: Step 2 of 3 · Audience, Back / Next / Generate
} from "@nucleux/structured-input";

<StructuredInputSlots
  slots={[
    { name: "audience", label: "Audience", options: [{ value: "execs", label: "Execs" }],
      suggested: "from the meeting invite" },
    { name: "length", label: "Length", placeholder: "3 bullets" },
    { name: "topic", label: "Topic", placeholder: "Yesterday's standup", wide: true },
  ]}
  freeform
  onSubmit={(values, freeform) => send(fill(template, values), freeform)}
/>

<StructuredInputTags
  triggers={[{ trigger: "@", label: "Person", suggestions: ["sam", "priya"] }, { trigger: "p:", label: "Project" }]}
  onSubmit={(parts, text) => send(text)}
/>

<StructuredInputWizard steps={["Intent", "Audience", "Tone"]} description="Who is the brief for?" onSubmit={generate}>
  {/* the current step's fields */}
</StructuredInputWizard>
```

Rules the components follow: plain labels; a freeform override; **no field is ever required before
sending**; agent-suggested values are marked “Suggested” (with why) and become “Edited by you” once
changed — never changed back. The single-choice question follows the radio-group keyboard pattern
(arrow keys move and select).

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/suggested-prompts

Suggested Prompts — smart, context-aware preset actions to jumpstart engagement — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

A few ready-made prompts that answer "what do I type?" without blocking the
composer. Choosing one hands its prompt to `onSelect` — place it in the
composer as editable text; never send it.

## Exports

- **`SuggestedPrompts`** — the set (`items` + `onSelect`, or compose children)
- **`SuggestedPrompt`** — one suggestion (a button; `icon`, `description`, `selected`)
- Types: `SuggestedPromptsProps`, `SuggestedPromptProps`, `SuggestedPromptItem`, `SuggestedPromptsVariant`, `SuggestedPromptsAfterSelect`

## Variants

| `variant` | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `chip-row` (default) | Pills above the composer in an empty thread. |
| `card-list` | Stacked cards with a supporting line, in an assistant panel. |
| `contextual-tooltip` | A dark bubble by the selection or cursor with one action; `onDismiss` adds × and Escape. |

## Behaviour

- `items` are strings or `{ id?, title, prompt?, description?, icon? }`; `onSelect(prompt, item)` gets the fuller `prompt` when there is one.
- Capped at `max` (5).
- `afterSelect`: `"keep"` (default), `"mark"` (others stay, the chosen one gets `aria-pressed`; control it with `selectedId`) or `"remove"` (remove once tapped).
- With `items` the set is a list named by `label` ("Try asking:"), or "Suggested prompts".
- Hide the set once the person types (the `hidden` attribute, or don't render it). `InitialCta` does this for you.

## Usage

```tsx
import { SuggestedPrompts } from "@nucleux/suggested-prompts";

<SuggestedPrompts
  label="Try asking:"
  items={[
    { title: "Find unresolved decisions", prompt: "Find the unresolved decisions blocking the September release." },
    "Draft a follow-up to Acme Corp",
    "Which accounts need attention?",
  ]}
  onSelect={(prompt) => { setDraft(prompt); composerRef.current?.focus(); }}
/>
```

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/suggested-prompts @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

packages.name: suggestions
packages.description:
Context-aware quick-action chips that save the person forming, typing and
submitting the obvious next step: above the composer as starters or quick
edits ("compose"), under an answer as follow-ups ("follow-up", marked ↳),
or as a floating toolbar on highlighted content ("selection"). At most three
verb-labelled chips; the row can be marked as the agent's (`label`), explain
itself behind an info toggle (`reason`) and be dismissed (button or Escape).
Choosing a chip only calls `onSelect` — it never sends — and the row can
then show a one-line confirmation with Undo, a dismissed or no-longer-relevant
line, a loading line or an error with Retry, through `status`. Arrow keys,
Home and End move between chips.

# @nucleux/suggestions

Suggestions — quick-action chips above the composer, under an answer or on a selection that add to the request, never send it — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

Context-aware chips that turn the likely next step into a tap. At most three,
labelled with verbs. They can be marked as the agent's ("Aria suggests"),
explain themselves behind an info toggle and be dismissed. Choosing one never
sends: it is appended after the person's own words, stays editable, and is
confirmed in one line with Undo.

## Exports

- **`Suggestions`** — the chip row and its status lines
- **`SuggestionsComposer`** — the row wired to `OpenInput`: pause before offering, append with Undo, dismiss, withdraw when no longer relevant, optional async loading
- Helpers shared with the Material 3 twin: `appendSuggestion`, `handleSuggestionsKeyDown`, `useSuggestions`, `useSuggestionsComposer`, `suggestionsMessages`, `suggestionKey`
- Types: `SuggestionsProps`, `SuggestionsComposerProps`, `SuggestionItem`, `SuggestionsVariant`, `SuggestionsStatus`, `SuggestionsMessages`

## Variants

| `variant` | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `compose` (default) | Chips just above the composer: starters or quick edits. |
| `follow-up` | Under an answer: what to ask next (marked ↳). |
| `selection` | A floating toolbar of actions on highlighted content (`role="toolbar"`). |

## States (`status`)

`available` (chips) · `loading` · `error` (Retry via `onRetry`) · `accepted` (Undo via `onUndo`) · `dismissed` · `irrelevant` · `idle` (renders nothing).

## Behaviour

- `label` gives the row a visible heading and names the group; without it, pass `aria-label`.
- `reason` sits behind an info button (`aria-expanded`). `onDismiss` adds a close button; Escape dismisses too.
- `actionLabel` prefixes each chip's accessible name ("Add to prompt: Include unresolved blockers").
- Arrow keys move between chips, Home/End jump to the ends; every chip is also a Tab stop.
- `pendingId` marks a chip whose action is running (spinner, `aria-busy`).
- No model calls: suggestions are data (`suggestions`) or an async `loadSuggestions(draft, { signal })` the app supplies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { SuggestionsComposer } from "@nucleux/suggestions";

<SuggestionsComposer
  label="Aria suggests"
  reason="Release summaries are read to decide what still needs attention."
  suggestions={[
    { label: "Include unresolved blockers" },
    { label: "Group the work by owner" },
    { label: "Compare with the August release" },
  ]}
  isRelevant={(draft) => /release/i.test(draft)}
  onSubmit={send}
/>
```

```tsx
import { Suggestions } from "@nucleux/suggestions";

<Suggestions variant="follow-up" aria-label="Suggested follow-ups"
  suggestions={[{ label: "Why Acme?" }, { label: "Draft outreach" }]} onSelect={(s) => ask(s.label)} />
```

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/suggestions @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/templates

Templates — fill-in-the-blank prompt scaffolds that turn vague intent into a good question — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

Structured prompts that capture good prompting: a sentence with named slots,
a list of fully written prompts, or a library grouped by domain. Nothing runs
until the person picks "Use this prompt" or a template.

## Exports

- **`Templates`** — fill-in-the-blank (`fill-blanks`): a form with inline slot fields
- **`TemplatesList`** — prefilled list (`prefilled-list`): one-tap prompts
- **`TemplatesBrowser`** — categorised browser (`categorized-browser`): vertical tabs per category
- Types: `TemplatesProps`, `PromptSegment`, `PromptSlot`, `TemplatesListProps`, `TemplatesListItem`, `TemplatesBrowserProps`, `TemplatesCategory`

## Behaviour

- `segments` mix literal strings and slots `{ slot, placeholder, label?, options?, required? }`. `options` give native type-ahead; the field stays free text.
- Required slots are counted ("1 blank left", `aria-live`) and the submit waits for them. Empty optional slots fall back to their placeholder.
- `onComplete(prompt, values)` gets the interpolated sentence. `TemplatesList`/`TemplatesBrowser` call `onSelect(prompt, item[, category])`.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Templates, TemplatesList, TemplatesBrowser } from "@nucleux/templates";

<Templates
  segments={[
    "Summarise ", { slot: "meeting", placeholder: "meeting", options: ["the standup", "the board review"], required: true },
    " in ", { slot: "length", placeholder: "3 bullets" },
    " for ", { slot: "audience", placeholder: "execs" }, ".",
  ]}
  onComplete={(prompt) => setDraft(prompt)}
/>

<TemplatesList aria-label="Templates" items={["Draft a follow-up to the at-risk accounts"]} onSelect={setDraft} />
```

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/templates @nucleux/tokens
```
