# @nucleux/visual-input

Visual Input — attach images, screenshots, or videos as part of the ask — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/visual-input @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { VisualInput, type VisualInputFile } from "@nucleux/visual-input";

const [files, setFiles] = useState<VisualInputFile[]>([]);

<VisualInput
  variant="paste-chip"            // "drag-drop" | "paste-chip" | "camera-capture"
  files={files}
  onFilesChange={setFiles}
  maxSize={20 * 1024 * 1024}
  maxFiles={4}
  seeText="Aria will see this when you send"
  unsupportedText="Aria can read images (PNG, JPG, HEIC)."
>
  <OpenInput … />                 {/* the composer the visual is paired with */}
</VisualInput>
```

- **Sources:** `sources={["upload", "paste", "camera"]}` — only what the product allows. Upload covers the
  browse button and drag-and-drop; paste picks up images pasted anywhere inside the component (plain-text
  paste is untouched); camera uses `<input type="file" accept="image/*" capture>`.
- **Limits:** `accept`, `maxSize`, `maxFiles`, `multiple`. Refused files are listed in an alert that says
  why and what can be used, and reported through `onReject`.
- **Never auto-sends.** The component only manages files; your app sends them with the prompt.
- **Per-file state:** set `status: "reading" | "error"` and `error` on a file to show a working or failed chip.

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

a clearly lit capturing state (waveform or pulsing stop button, clock, live

# @nucleux/voice-input

VoiceInput — a live dictation bar with a waveform — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/voice-input @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { VoiceInput } from "@nucleux/voice-input";

<VoiceInput
  variant="transcript-stream"       // "waveform" (default) | "mic-button" | "transcript-stream"
  state={state}                     // "idle" | "recording" | "paused" | "transcribing" | "error"
  duration="0:14"
  transcript={finalWords}
  interimTranscript={wordsStillBeingHeard}
  listeningLabel="Aria is listening"
  onStart={start}
  onPause={pause}
  onResume={resume}
  onCancel={discard}                // typed text stays
  onConfirm={stop}                  // puts the transcript in the field — never sends
  onRetry={retry}
/>
```

Speech recognition is the app's job; this component renders the states. Keep the verbs distinct:
**Pause** (mic off, keep progress), **Resume**, **Stop** (end, keep what was said, do not send) and
**Cancel** (discard this recording). State changes are announced through a polite live region, and the
waveform, caret and pulse stop under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux

# @nucleux/voice-tone

Voice & Tone — say how the reply should sound (named presets, a rules list, a sample line), as a Tone chip or a Tone row in Request settings, never editing the prompt — Nucleux agentic UI for React.

Part of **[Nucleux](https://github.com/intelligaia-open-labs/nucleux)** — agentic UI components for React. Install a single component, or the full kit via [`@nucleux/react`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/react).

A Material 3 twin with the same API ships as [`@nucleux/md3-voice-tone`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nucleux/md3-voice-tone).

## Exports

- **`VoiceTone`** — `variant="settings"` (default): a preferences panel with tone presets, a rules list and a sample sentence. `variant="composer"`: a composer with a Tone chip that opens the tone picker (cards, list, segmented or slider; sample line; recommendation marked, never applied; “Or describe a tone”), then names the choice and can be changed or removed with Undo. `variant="chip"`: the chip and picker alone, for your own composer.
- **`useVoiceTone`** — the shared state and keyboard model (used by the Material 3 twin).
- **`defaultVoiceTones`**, **`defaultVoiceToneRules`**, **`VOICE_TONE_CUSTOM`**
- Types: `VoiceToneProps`, `VoiceToneOption`, `VoiceToneRule`, `VoiceToneSetting`, `VoiceToneVariant`, `VoiceToneLayout`, `VoiceToneNotice`, `VoiceToneState`

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @nucleux/voice-tone @nucleux/tokens
```

`react` / `react-dom` are peer dependencies.

## Usage

```tsx
import { VoiceTone, defaultVoiceToneRules } from "@nucleux/voice-tone";

// Preferences: set once, applied to every reply.
<VoiceTone defaultValue="professional" rules={defaultVoiceToneRules} onValueChange={saveTone} onRulesChange={saveRules} />

// In the composer: the tone travels with the request as a setting — the prompt is never edited.
<VoiceTone variant="composer" onSubmit={(text, setting) => send(text, { tone: setting })} />
```

Requires the theme once in your app: `import "@nucleux/tokens/styles.css";`
and the Tailwind preset from `@nucleux/tokens/preset`.

## License

MIT © Nucleux
